content.text:
GUEST:
Dr. Lisa Tzu-Fang Su is President and CEO of AMD (2014-present) and Chair of AMD (2022-present).
She joined AMD in 2012 as senior vice president and general manager of Global Business Units, and was promoted to president and CEO in 2014.
She became Chair in February 2022 after the Xilinx acquisition closed.
She holds a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from MIT and was previously vice president of IBM's Semiconductor Research and Development Center.
Before AMD, she was Chief Technology Officer and VP and General Manager of Networking and Multimedia at Freescale Semiconductor.

COMPANY:
Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD) is a fabless semiconductor company.
It sells into three reporting segments: Data Center (EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI accelerators, Pensando networking), Client and Gaming (Ryzen processors, Radeon graphics, semi-custom console APUs), and Embedded (Xilinx FPGAs and adaptive SoCs).
Its portfolio includes EPYC server CPUs, Instinct data-center GPUs, Ryzen client processors, Radeon graphics, embedded products, networking technology, and ROCm AI software.
It is listed on Nasdaq. Market quote for October 26, 2026: $531.28, previous close $516.79, up 2.8% on the day.

RECENT:
1. July 22, 2026 - Strategic partnership with Anthropic. AMD and Anthropic announced a partnership to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD Instinct MI450 Series GPUs in AMD Helios rack-scale solutions, with first gigawatt beginning in first half of 2027.
As part of that announcement, AMD committed to make a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic.

2. August 4, 2026 - Q2 2026 financial results. AMD reported record Q2 revenue of $11.5 billion, with Data Center revenue of $6.7 billion accounting for 58% of total revenue.
Non-GAAP earnings were $1.66 per share, beating Wall Street consensus of $1.62 but below the $1.69 Whisper Number estimate.
For Q3 the company guided revenue of approximately $13 billion plus or minus $300 million.

3. September 28, 2026 - Agreement to acquire World Labs. AMD said it would acquire Fei-Fei Li's AI startup World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at $8.2 billion.
The startup builds AI models of three dimensional spaces and tools for training robots, and the deal is expected to close by the end of 2026.
Li is set to join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting directly to Su.

4. October 12, 2026 - Introduction of AMD Helion. AMD introduced the AMD Helion agentic AI rack, an open blueprint for agentic AI infrastructure based on an Open Compute Project spec-design and powered by AMD compute.
Examples include a CPU-only rack with up to 32,768 CPU cores and an enterprise configuration combining AMD EPYC processors with AMD Instinct MI350P GPUs.

NUMBERS:
- Q2 2026 revenue $11.536 billion, up 50% year over year. Source: AMD Q2 2026 earnings release via Nasdaq / FinanceFeeds, August 4, 2026.
- Q2 2026 Data Center revenue $6.7 billion, up 107% year over year, 58% of total revenue. Source: AMD Q2 2026 earnings reporting, August 2026.
- Q2 2026 non-GAAP EPS $1.66, GAAP diluted EPS $1.38, up 156% year over year on GAAP basis. Source: AMD Q2 2026 results, August 4, 2026.
- Q3 2026 guidance: revenue approximately $13.0 billion plus or minus $300 million. Source: AMD Q2 earnings call / guidance, August 4, 2026.
- World Labs acquisition value approximately $8.2 billion in AMD stock, expected close by end of 2026 subject to approvals. Source: AMD announcement, September 28, 2026, via Reuters.
- Anthropic partnership: up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 Series GPUs plus AMD equity investment up to $5 billion. Source: AMD press release, July 22, 2026.
- Helion platform: up to 32,768 CPU cores in CPU-only rack example. Source: AMD announcement coverage, October 12, 2026.
- AMD share price $531.28 on Nasdaq as of October 26, 2026, 52-week range $188.22 to $658.52. Source: market_quote via Yahoo Finance, October 26, 2026.

QUESTIONS:
Explain for a non-technical audience how agentic AI changes what a data-center rack has to do, and where Helion fits in.
Critics argue gigawatt announcements and equity-linked AI deals pull forward demand that may be slow to convert to revenue - how do you answer that concern for AMD?
Looking toward first Helios-based gigawatt deployments in late 2026 and first half of 2027, what milestones should viewers watch to judge progress?
You personally led AMD's turn toward high-performance computing more than a decade ago - what lesson from that period guides you most in this AI build-out?

CAUTION:
World Labs $8.2 billion deal completion by end of 2026 is pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, not yet confirmed closed.
Anthropic first-gigawatt deployment in H1 2027 and OpenAI/Meta gigawatt frameworks starting H2 2026 are forward commitments, not delivered revenue - treat as planned.
Third-party estimates of cumulative revenue from gigawatt deals and of AMD's share of data-center AI accelerator revenue (e.g. 5% to 7% in 2026) are analyst estimates, not AMD guidance.
Reports of a roughly 10% supply-price increase in Q4 2026 trace to supply-chain firms via tech press, not confirmed by AMD - do not present as company policy.
Market capitalization near $1 trillion claims in some coverage could not be confirmed for broadcast date - use current market_quote instead.
Q3 2026 results are scheduled for November 3, 2026 - Q3 guidance figures remain outlook, not results.
